methodological_rigor.justification: Preclinical mouse model study with multiple transgenic/knockout lines (BELMO, Slc12a2IEC-cKO, Slc12a4IEC-cKO, Zeb2) across two CRC models (AOM/DSS inducible, Zeb2 spontaneous). Blinded scoring (stool, endoscopy), standardized protocols (MEICS scoring), appropriate statistical tests (one-way ANOVA, log-rank Mantel-Cox). Limitations: small cohorts (n=3-10 per group), primarily null findings, no a priori power calculations reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical mechanistic study (LoE 5) investigating efferocytosis in colorectal cancer using mouse models. Limited direct translational relevance; primarily hypothesis-generating negative results. While addresses important biological mechanism (apoptotic cell clearance in tumor microenvironment), null findings reduce immediate clinical impact compared to positive mechanistic discoveries.

reporting_quality.justification: Preclinical animal study with detailed methodology including mouse genetic background (C57BL/6), housing/environmental conditions, ethical approval (EC file numbers specified), treatment protocols (AOM/DSS dosing, timing), outcome measures (MEICS scoring, TUNEL, RT-qPCR, ELISA), and statistical approaches. ARRIVE principles evident. However, no statement on data/code availability; reproducibility dependent on institutional protocols and animal facility access.

novelty_literature.justification: Meaningful but incremental contribution evaluating complementary efferocytosis-enhancing (BELMO) and efferocytosis-reducing (Slc12a2/Slc12a4 knockout) approaches in CRC. Extends prior in vitro work (Morioka et al. BELMO, Perry et al. Slc12a channels) to in vivo CRC models. Primary novelty is in testing specific hypothesis; negative results valuable for field but not discovery-level.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear hypothesis statement, detailed methodological descriptions (mouse crosses, AOM/DSS protocol, imaging techniques, gene expression analysis), logical presentation of results across three complementary genetic models, and thorough discussion contextualizing negative findings with prior literature. Figures and figure legends comprehensive with sample sizes and statistical tests clearly stated.

key_strengths: Three complementary genetic approaches (BELMO-overexpressing, Slc12a2-knockout, Slc12a4-knockout) tested across two independent CRC models (AOM/DSS inducible and Zeb2 spontaneous) systematically assessing efferocytosis mechanisms

Multiple outcome measures (survival, body weight, stool score, endoscopic MEICS scoring, histopathology, cytokine quantification by RT-qPCR and ELISA, TUNEL apoptosis detection) providing comprehensive disease assessment
Appropriate blinding strategies (stool scorer blinded to genotype; senior radiologists blinded to treatment allocation for endoscopy scoring)
Clear technical documentation of transgenic generation, genotyping validation, and expression confirmation by RT-qPCR

Honest negative findings with thoughtful discussion of potential explanations (timing of tissue sampling, cell type targeting limitations, functional redundancy) rather than overselling minimal trends
key_concerns: Primarily null findings across all three genetic models and two disease models limiting novelty and impact; no significant alterations in disease progression despite detectable modulation of efferocytic parameters
Small cohort sizes (n=3-10 per group) underpowered for detecting modest but potentially biologically relevant effects; no a priori power calculations or sample size justifications provided

Key limitation acknowledged but incompletely addressed: targeting intestinal epithelial cells may not capture full efferocytosis biology; recruited macrophages and tumor-associated macrophages likely more important but not targeted

Slc12a2 knockout mice showed increased apoptotic cell clearance (lower TUNEL staining) but no corresponding changes in pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, suggesting sampling timing may not capture relevant inflammatory windows
No data/code availability statement; limited external reproducibility without access to transgenic mouse lines and detailed institutional protocols
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competently executed preclinical study with appropriate methodology but primarily negative findings of modest scope. Suitable for Tier 3 (4-9.9 JIF) emphasis on negative/null results in carefully designed experiments. Minor revisions should strengthen power analysis discussion and propose specific future directions for macrophage-targeted studies.
